newsitem.title: UK: Nervous London gold sits on interim support.
newsitem.headline: Nervous London gold sits on interim support.

text.p: Gold prices balanced precariously at a recent support level on Thursday morning and dealers said they could soon topple towards the key $340 an ounce threshold to extend the slide that they began last year.
Bullion was fixed at $343.40 an ounce, unchanged from Wednesday afternoon in cautious early trading.
Support at around $343 an ounce has emerged this week, but it was unlikely to prop up prices for long, dealers said.
Continued strength in the dollar was expected to encourage holders of gold to cash in while limiting fresh investment.
"Physical demand has dropped off in Europe. The high dollar against the mark has made gold much more expensive," a European analyst noted.
The $340 level, a key low from 1993, was a reasonable target in the very near future, dealers said.
"We may see it as soon as today or tomorrow," one said.
On the demand side, gold's decline by some $25 an ounce since the start of the year has boosted gold demand in the Middle East and Asia, according to the World Gold Council.
But increased physical offtake has been unable to offset the market's overwhelmingly bearish tone, deepened by fears that central banks will continue selling their reserves this year.
Fresh institutional selling last week was attributed by some dealers to a central bank, although others have pointed the finger at gold producers panicking about gold's steep decline.

"With sentiment favouring an interest rate cut in Australia, coupled with recent weakness in the Australian dollar, we would guess the incentives are there to stimulate producer selling," said analyst Larry Kaplan of Flemings Global Mining Group.
Technical analysts noted that gold was trying to consolidate after sinking to fresh 3-1/4 year lows earlier this week.
But any move higher would stall at $346-$347, they added.
Silver prices were modestly firmer at $4.88/$4.89 an ounce, an advance of three cents from Wednesday's Lodnon close. It was expected to remain in a $4.80-$5.00 range for the time being.

But dealers said it had more upside potential as long as Russian producers and Japanese consumers failed to agree sales agreements for the year. Japanese dealers have been covering there needs in the spot market, driving up pricess
Platinum, though downtrending with gold overall, was up $1.00 at $351.25/$352.25.
